newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Singleton has offers for TEN stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Singleton has offers for TEN stake.

text.p: John Singleton Advertising Ltd (JSA) said it wanted to sell its five percent stake in TEN Group Ltd, Australia's third-ranked television network, and gave other founding investors 30 days to make bids before it looked elsewhere.
JSA said it wanted at least A$13 per share for its 4.55 million shares, valuing TEN at A$1.18 billion.
"We have been approached by certain institutions who are interested in picking up the parcel. We have them as potential suitors," JSA director and lawyer Geoff Levy told Reuters.
Levy said JSA had the options of selling its stake into a unit trust which would be underwritten, selling to institutions, or selling the shares into a share market float.
Of the three, Levy said JSA preferred a float.
"We would be happier (with a float) because we would get more than A$13 but we are not relying on it," he said.

A number of other TEN shareholders, including Izzy Asper's CanWest Global Communications Inc, have so far blocked the float proposal due to a hefty capital gains tax liability and the inferred reduction in his 57.5 percent economic interest.

CanWest has a 15 percent voting interest in TEN, the difference being due to the fact that the company is foreign-owned and therefore cannot have more than a 15 percent stake without government approval.
The government's broadcasting authority has ruled that the economic interest does not mean Asper controls TEN.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said this week that CanWest and Telecasters North Queensland Ltd, which has a 40 percent voting stake, had also opposed JSA's unit trust proposal. Singleton and other minority shareholders have been seeking a profitable exit from TEN for most of 1996.
The TEN shareholder agreement contains a pre-emptive rights clause which gives other shareholders 30 days to bid for TEN shares if they are put up for sale.

"We wouldn't have put in the price we have or put in the (stock exchange) notice unless we were clearly confident we had a buyer lined up for the eventuation of none of the shareholders taking it," Levy said.
TEN has proved to be highly profitable for its shareholders in the last few years, with 1995/96 pre-tax profit rising by 49 percent to A$151.1 million.
Levy said brokers were lining up to be involved in a float.
He said a share market float may still happen, sometime next year if not later in 1996.
"It still may happen. The shareholders have never stopped using their best endeavours."
In terms of audience share, TEN ranks third behind Seven Network Ltd and Kerry Packer's Nine Network Ltd, owned by his listed Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd.
The network has market leadership, however, in the young adult sector which is keenly sought by advertisers.
